missing: A side-by-side of specific NAS models (Synology BeeStation/DS224+, UGREEN DH2300/DH4300 Plus, ZimaCube, QNAP) priced with drives against $9.99/month iCloud+ 2TB, judged on the things a four-iPhone family actually needs: per-person auto photo upload from the iOS app, remote access away from home, HEIC/Live Photo handling, shared folders, Mac Time Machine; plus an explicit list of what iCloud does that no NAS does (full iPhone device backup, Messages/Keychain/Notes sync, Shared Library, Hide My Email, Private Relay) and whether to keep a cheaper iCloud tier alongside.
why: No major reviewer or authority tests a NAS as an iCloud 2TB replacement here. The only famous name (Gizmodo) is about cloud services, not NAS. Two pages address the question directly: Apple Scoop (spec-based, admits no testing) and RottenWiFi (UGREEN-only). The rest are maker blogs from Synology and Zima, affiliate roundups with unverifiable 'tested' claims, a bare Reddit question, and generic storage explainers. A focused page comparing named models with drive-inclusive prices, the iOS-app workflow for a multi-person household, and a clear what-you-lose list would stand out.
